assessment.overall_rationale: The two module sets are strongly congruent one-to-one: L1↔R1 (Phase II bile acid/steroid sulfation/conjugation), L2↔R2 (peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation and lipid droplet homeostasis), and L3↔R3 (cysteine/taurine/sulfur-nitrogen catabolism with hepatocyte aging signature) each share core mechanism, dominant genes, and key regulators, while all cross-pairs are biologically distinct processes linked only by incidental shared regulators or a single overlapping gene with divergent roles.

pair_scores.rationale: Both describe the same hepatic Phase II sulfotransferase/glutathione-conjugation program for bile acids and hydroxysteroids, sharing Sult2a-family, Gsta3, Akr1c6, Aldh1a1 genes and Abcg5/Tpst1 regulators, with L1 additionally naming Cyp2c50 and explicit Nrf2/CAR upstream control.

Both are hepatocyte metabolic programs and share the Cyb5b gene, but L1's mechanism is xenobiotic/steroid conjugation while R2's is peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation and lipid droplet biology, and Cyb5b is assigned a different functional role in each.
L1's xenobiotic/steroid conjugation mechanism and R3's sulfur/nitrogen catabolism and aging signature are distinct processes with no shared genes and only an incidental shared Abcg5 regulator.
L2's peroxisomal fatty acid catabolism and R1's Phase II sulfation/conjugation program share no genes, regulators, or mechanistic overlap beyond generic hepatocyte metabolism.

Both center on peroxisomal/microsomal fatty acid and lipid-droplet handling with near-identical core genes (Hao2, Aldh3a2, Fitm1) and the Dgat2 regulator, with R2 adding Psmd1/Cyb5b as a minor refinement.
L2's fatty acid/lipid aldehyde catabolism and R3's sulfur/nitrogen catabolism and aging signature share no genes or mechanistic overlap.
L3's cysteine/taurine and nitrogen metabolism program is mechanistically unrelated to R1's bile acid/steroid sulfation program, with only a peripheral shared Insig1 regulator.
L3's sulfur amino acid catabolism and R2's peroxisomal lipid oxidation/droplet program are distinct mechanisms that only share the peripheral Insig1 regulator.

Both describe the Cdo1-driven cysteine/taurine catabolism axis coupled to Rgn-marked hepatocyte aging, sharing Cdo1, Rgn, Sord, Alad genes and the G6pc regulator, with R3 adding an explicit Car5a/urea-cycle refinement already implied in L3's summary.
